answer: On the tide the lagoon vault opens, holding one escrow per real customer: someone with a live need posts their own money against it, and the vault pays only the agent that actually discharges that need, once the customer confirms - the escrow is spent for good and never returned. The scarce per-head input is that person's real need and their own money: unprintable, unlendable to a sibling head, consumed once filled, so a farm's tenth head needs a tenth still-unfilled need, while honest agents take the easy needs first. Two agents claiming one escrow void it and pay the honest pool.
